notes: British campaigns of 1900-02 (Aro Expedition) broke Aro power; Arochukwu taken Dec 1901 and the Aro submitted to the Southern Nigeria government in 1902. Core then administered by the British protectorate.

Latial Iron Age is a material-culture phase; Latin settlements from 10th c. BCE continue into archaic Rome and Latin cities. c. 580 BCE is a phase boundary (end of Latial IVB), not a recorded break. Sources thin.

source2: Osborne, Massa, Sahin, Erpehlivan, Bachhuber, 'The city of Hartapu: results of the Turkmen-Karahoyuk Intensive Survey Project', Anatolian Studies 70, 2020 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/anatolian-studies/article/city-of-hartapu-results-of-the-turkmenkarahoyuk-intensive-survey-project/B136B9F3C460ACFF25660B2B5E4C6E11
notes: No documented break c. 900 BCE; Tabal is itself a Neo-Hittite state and Turkmen-Karahoyuk remained the regional political centre from late 2nd to mid-1st millennium BCE. Konya Plain 12th-10th c. poorly documented; Hartapu's date disputed.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Qi, ancient state, China [771-221 BC]' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Qi-ancient-state-China-771-221-BC
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'China: The Qin empire (221-207 BCE)' - https://www.britannica.com/place/China/The-Qin-empire-221-207-bce
notes: Qin conquered and absorbed Qi in 221 BCE, the last Warring State, completing unification; database 222 and Western Han candidate are off. Yan-led occupation of 284-279 BCE lies outside the 50-year window.

After Queen Arwa's death (1138) Sulayhid lands passed to the Zurayids amid rival petty dynasties; Saladin's brother Turan-Shah conquered Yemen in 1173-74 and the capital moved to Ta'izz. External conquest of a fragmented core.

After the Six Garrisons revolt (523) and Erzhu Rong's 528 seizure of Luoyang, the state was divided among its generals in 534: Xiaowu fled to Yuwen Tai, Gao Huan moved the court to Ye. Eastern Wei arguably continuity (T0).

successor: Hallstatt B2-3 (Late Bronze Age Urnfield phase)
notes: Chronological sub-phase of the Late Bronze Age Urnfield complex, no central authority; sources stress persistence of pottery and metal forms into the Early Iron Age, no break c. 900. Conventional Ha A begins c. 1200 BCE, so database start looks late.

successor: Seleucid Empire (Seleucus I), then Ptolemy Keraunos at Lysimacheia
notes: Execution of Agathocles (c. 284-282) triggered city revolts and defections; Seleucus invaded and killed Lysimachus at Corupedium, 281 BCE. Seleucus was murdered near Lysimacheia months later by Ptolemy Keraunos, who took Thrace and Macedon.

successor: Republic of India (Garo Hills district, Assam)
source1: West Garo Hills District Administration, 'History' - https://westgarohills.gov.in/history/
notes: Tura-based district administration created under British rule continued under India after 1947; the Garo Hills district persisted until split in 1976. No break found at 1956; end date looks arbitrary. Evidence thin.

source1: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'ELAM i. The history of Elam' - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
notes: Igihalkid line (to c. 1210 BCE) followed by the Shutrukid dynasty as kings of Anshan and Susa: dynastic change within the Elamite state, no known foreign conquest. Database successor 'Neo-Assyrian Empire' is wrong.
